title: I made a browser game where you can’t grind your character. You have to improve in real life.
author: SecondFew4212
selftext:
Simply, the idea is you pick one promise for 90 days:

Read 10 pages, Go for a walk, Quit a bad habit, etc..

Every day you keep that promise, you forge another layer onto your shield.

And that same shield is your actual strength in the game. So you get stronger by keeping a real life promise.

I’m building this solo and trying to figure out if this connection between real life and the game is actually motivating, or just sounds good in my head.

No registration to start, and all 90 levels are free now.

Check it here: [90to90.com](http://90to90.com)

Would this make you more likely to stick to something for 90 days, or would you lose interest after a week?

comments.author: Raqnarock
comments.body: Its actually an interesting idea. Making two groups of people with them picking up a habit and have one group play the game and the other group not play the game and see whether there is a difference in success.

replies.author: SecondFew4212
replies.body: Love this idea! A proper A/B test would definitely give the clearest proof. Hope to run an experiment like that once more users jump in. Thanks for the great insight!

replies.author: Raqnarock
replies.body: Sure, and you enjoy developing it!

replies.author: SecondFew4212
replies.body: Thanks! Glad you like the concept.
